conviction_note: Both direct insurance lead-gen peers that reported after TREE last spoke beat their own Q3 guides by 7-10% on revenue and 15-19% on EBITDA. Insurance is about two thirds of TREE revenue, so TREE's Q3 revenue probably lands above the $330m guide midpoint and consensus. TREE has moved only about +9% on those two days against +17-21% for the peers, which is why p_up is above 50. It is held to 57 because this name fell 20-22% on each of its last two prints: in Q1 revenue beat and guidance was raised, and the stock was sold on profit and margin. Management guided H2 insurance margins flat at the compressed Q2 level. That gives 0.14 x 18 = +2.5. The findings sum to +4.5 because they are sized one at a time and are not fitted to that number.

positioning_check: FINRA short interest via equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/tree/shortinterest): 1,052,405 shares on the 2026-10-15 settlement, 7.5% of 14.04m shares outstanding, 4.25 days to cover. That is up from 881k (2.8 DTC) on 09-30 and 846k on 08-31; it was 1.65m on 08-14. Float is materially smaller than shares outstanding because the Lebda estate, Lebda Family Holdings and Richard Balot together hold about 25%+ (13G/A, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001434621/000168316826005987/primary_doc.xml), so short interest is roughly 10-11% of float. Moderate and building, not extremely crowded. Options: the chain is unusable (ATM spread 86% of mid, skew rejected at 40 vol points), so there is no usable skew. ATM IV is 90.5% at 17 DTE, which netted of 47% realised vol implies roughly a 17% event move; put/call OI is 0.78. Tape: +13.6% over 20d and +7.1% over 5d, still -58.7% from the 52-week high. The stock rose from $24.35 on 09-30 (Form 4 price) to $27.99 intraday on 11-03.

findings.finding: TREE's two direct insurance lead-gen peers both reported Q3 2026 after TREE last spoke, and both beat their own guides by a wide margin. MediaAlpha (10-28): revenue $375.9m vs a $330-355m guide (+10% vs midpoint) and adj EBITDA $39.5m vs $32-35m (+18%), with carriers 'competing aggressively for new policies' in auto and home. EverQuote (11-02): revenue $218.1m vs $198-208m (+7%), VMD $62.6m vs $56-59m (+8%), adj EBITDA $35.5m vs $28-31m (+20%), with VMD margin flat YoY at about 28.7%. TREE Insurance was $209m of $313m Q2 revenue. If TREE's insurance beats by half the peers' margin (+3-5% on about $215m), Q3 revenue lands about $338-345m against a $330m consensus that equals the guide midpoint and was set before these prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (04-30): revenue $327m beat about $316m consensus and FY guide was raised, yet the stock fell 21.7% on a profit/Home-margin miss. Q2 2026 (07-29): revenue +25% YoY with Insurance +42%, but Consumer missed and the Q3 guide was below consensus, -19.6%. Revenue beats on insurance alone have not been paid on the last two prints; the stock trades on VMM/EBITDA and segment profit.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. TREE closed +5.7% on 10-29, when MAX rose 20.6%, and is about +3.3% intraday on 11-03 while EVER is +17.4% (Yahoo chart, 11-03 13:00 ET). Revenue consensus still sits exactly at the guide midpoint ($329.8m). If the market had fully carried the peer beats into TREE, TREE would have moved with the peers, and the revenue consensus would sit above the guide.
findings.independence: MediaAlpha Q3 2026 8-K, a different company and document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818383/000181838326000263/maxq32026-earningsreleasex.htm (its guide: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818383/000181838326000198/maxq22026-earningsreleasex.htm). Both peers are proxies for TREE's QuoteWizard, not TREE's own numbers. TREE's Q2 insurance fell 6% QoQ while peers grew, so share or margin management may differ.

findings.finding: Carrier demand extends into Q4 in both peers' outlooks. MediaAlpha guides Q4 revenue $355-375m (+25% YoY at the midpoint), citing 'strong carrier growth investment'. EverQuote guides Q4 revenue $213-223m, saying carriers 'maintain strong underwriting profitability and an appetite for growth'. TREE's FY guide of $1.30-1.32bn implies Q4 revenue of about $340m at the midpoint (H1 $640m plus Q3 mid $330m). A peer-consistent insurance trend gives room for a raise or a firmed FY/Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: FY guide raised, stock -21.7% (the profit miss dominated). Q2 2026: FY guide trimmed and Q3 revenue guide below the $337m consensus, -19.6%. The guide line has been the swing factor on both recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: No sell-side revision to TREE's Q4 or FY numbers since the peer prints is visible. The $61 average target dates from early August (MarketBeat 2026-08-01). If this were priced, TREE's FY estimates would sit above the guide midpoint and the stock would have tracked the peers' +17-21% days.
findings.independence: Shares its documents with finding 1 (the MAX and EVER releases), but lands on a different line: the forward guide rather than the reported quarter. EverQuote Q4 guide in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001640428/000119312526443633/ever-ex99_1.htm. Proxy, not TREE's own guide.

findings.finding: Q2 insurance segment profit grew 25% on 42% revenue growth (margin about 23.9% vs 27.2% a year earlier). On the Q2 call management said H2 insurance margins would be broadly similar to Q2 because of traffic-cost and carrier competition. EverQuote, by contrast, held VMD margin flat YoY in Q3. So any TREE insurance revenue beat may come at compressed margin, the pattern this name was sold on in Q1 and Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both recent -20% prints were profit-quality misses: Home profit -24% in Q1, and Consumer profit -14% with EPS well below consensus in Q2. Revenue beats were not rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. It is the company's own guided margin, inside guidance, so this is sized small. What is not priced is whether EverQuote's flat-margin Q3 means TREE's traffic costs eased too. That is unknown and is why the range is wide.
findings.independence: Call summary: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/lendingtree-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-29/ (Simply Wall St via Webull, 2026-07-30, on margin pressure from traffic costs: https://www.webull.com/news/15318573486859264). Same company document family as the bar.

findings.finding: Small-business credit supply on the lender side was strong in Q3 2026. Enova reported small-business originations of about $1.8bn, +28% YoY, and its small-business receivables were +34% YoY at 09-30-2026. This is consistent with TREE's Q2 statement that small-business loan appetite on its network 'has since stabilized' after deteriorating through Q2, the line that caused the Q2 Consumer miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the Consumer/small-business miss drove the -19.6% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission. Enova is a lender, and TREE's Q2 weakness was borrower demand on its marketplace, so the read is indirect and few will connect it. The small-business share of Consumer is roughly a third, so the dollar effect is small.
findings.independence: Enova 10-Q for Q3 2026 (SB receivables +34%): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001529864/000119312526429122/enva-20260930.htm. Proxy only; the 1.8bn/+28% figure comes from a Webull call summary.

baseline_tension: No usable skew. The +13.6% 20d run-up already reflects part of the peer read-through, so the positive lean cuts partly into what is priced. The name's own history of selling revenue beats keeps p_up near 57.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its Q1 revenue beat and raise by 21.7%): peer-beat finding cut from +3.5 to +3.0, p_up 58 -> 57
'What has worked' (a peer's print landing after the company last spoke, leaving consensus stale) supports keeping the peer finding as the main one, not cutting it further
Rule 9 (segment net of rest): insurance is about 67%; Consumer is guided to stabilize and Home is about 14%, so no further change
Rule 7: short interest checked; moderate (about 10-11% of float), so the -1.0 margin finding is left as is
